title: Encomienda system on Hispaniola
summary: After Nicolas de Ovando arrived as governor in April 1502, a royal order of 20 December 1503 divided Indians among Spanish colonists, the basis of the encomienda. Colonists could use Indian labour, in practice often enslavement. With disease, abuse and violence, the system contributed to the collapse of the Taino population.

uncertainty.note: Start is Ovando's arrival (April 1502); the repartimiento order is dated 20 December 1503. End 1514 is when a Cambridge article places a major redistribution of communities to new encomenderos; the system continued after that.

where.modern_name: Island of Hispaniola (pin is Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, the colonial capital)
where.historical_name: Hispaniola, Spanish colony under governor Nicolas de Ovando

importance.justification: The first colonial labour-grant system in the Americas, a model for Spanish rule and a cause of Taino population collapse.

audience_note: Describes forced labour, enslavement and mass death of Indigenous people.

related.because: Spanish settlement of Hispaniola began after Columbus's first voyage.

reviewer_note: Sources disagree on the sequence: Encyclopedia.com and the Haiti study say Ovando's tenure replaced repartimiento with encomienda; the Dominican Republic study says the crown instituted encomienda in 1503. Taino population figures vary too widely (e.g. 500 vs 150 survivors by the mid-1500s) and are left out. The pin is the colonial capital for an island-wide process.
